text: Shows the four modes old_only, shadow, both and new_only, with forward transitions one step at a time in that order and no skipping, each made by a person.
States which engine charges and writes the ledger in each mode (old in old_only and shadow, new in both and new_only), and that the other engine never charges.

Gives both promotion gates: shadow to both needs 7 consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and at least 5,000 invoices compared; both to new_only needs 14 days with no unresolved mismatches plus Finance sign-off.

Shows rollback from shadow, both and new_only, always ending in old_only. Manual rollback is allowed at any time within the 35-day limit; automatic rollback (charge failures above 2% over 10 minutes) happens only in both or new_only.
Explains how a rollback avoids charging anyone twice and avoids dropping due charges.

Shows that rolling back from new_only requires the old engine to reprocess the skipped usage events, and that rollback from new_only is no longer possible from day 35, after which the old engine may be decommissioned.
States that the gates reset after a rollback and that the rollout must go through shadow again.
Delivered as a Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 with short notes before or after it covering mode behaviour, where state lives and failure handling.
